lines.text: Around 2012, reading Twitter was much harder than posting to it.
lines.say: Around twenty twelve, reading Twitter was much harder than posting to it.

lines.text: About 4,600 tweets a second went out, but timelines were loaded 300,000 times a second.
lines.say: About forty-six hundred tweets a second went out, but timelines were loaded three hundred thousand times a second.

lines.text: The simple way: when you open your timeline, look up everyone you follow and merge their tweets.
One read fans out into many lookups, and Twitter's first version struggled to keep up.
So they flipped it: each new tweet is copied into every follower's cached timeline.
Each tweet reaches 75 followers on average: 345,000 writes a second.
lines.say: Each tweet reaches seventy-five followers on average: three hundred forty-five thousand writes a second.

lines.text: But some accounts have over 30 million followers.
lines.say: But some accounts have over thirty million followers.

lines.text: So Twitter moved to a hybrid.
Most tweets are still copied when they're posted.
Celebrity tweets are fetched when you read, and merged in.
The lesson: a few outliers can decide your whole design.
